title: SteinerMineBench reference solution
description: The reference solution for one instance, produced by solve_reference.py. reference_cost on the raw track is the graded quantity; a submission's optimality gap is measured against it.

reference_type.description: 'exact' means the winning family's junction placement was independently recomputed from scratch and matched (see per_family[].exactness_check). 'best_known' means the winner uses a greedy or coordinate-descent search and may be improvable. 'unsolved' means no reference has been computed.

objective.description: Human-readable statement of exactly what reference_cost measures.

reference_cost.description: Raw voxel Steiner cost in dollars of the cheapest applicable family. The normative, graded quantity. Null iff reference_type is 'unsolved'.

reference_cost_buildable.description: Cost after deterministic geometric buildability post-processing (grade and turn-radius enforcement, spiral insertion). Secondary scoring track.

lower_bound.description: The RAW-track bound, kept under its v2.0.0 name and semantics. For the constrained and total tracks see lower_bounds.

lower_bounds.description: Per-track lower bounds. The raw track is bounded by the relaxation (pairwise divergence); the constrained and total tracks add a geometric floor derived from the grade limit, which is NOT valid on the raw track because an unconstrained network may descend at any angle.

gap_to_lower_bound.description: (reference_cost - lower_bound) / lower_bound on the RAW track. An upper bound on the true optimality gap of the raw reference.

bounds_recomputed_utc.description: When the bound blocks were last rewritten by solve_reference.py --recompute-bounds-only. The geometric floors need only metadata.json, so they can be re-derived and audited without re-solving.

support_class_length_m.description: Metres of drive in each Barton Q support class, keyed by the support_class strings in metadata.cost_model.tier_schedule.

exactness_check.description: Result of an independent recomputation that shares no code with the reference solver. Present only for families whose search is 'exact'.

method.description: The method that produced the strongest bound for this track. Every method that sets a value is provably valid; they differ in tightness, not soundness. Deliberately an open string rather than an enum: a closed enum makes every future bound a breaking schema change, and `components` has always been open. steinerbench.lower_bound.KNOWN_BOUND_METHODS lists what the suite currently emits and validate.py warns on anything else. Currently: pairwise_divergence, max_terminal_shortest_path, raw_relaxation, geometric_grade_floor, geometric_grade_floor+opex_floor, none. WITHDRAWN in v2.1.0: wong_dual_ascent (never competitive on a dense voxel lattice; validate.py now fails on it).

valid.description: Must be true. A bound that does not provably lower-bound the optimum over ALL applicable topology families must not ship.

track.description: Which cost track this bound applies to. A bound is only meaningful against its own track's cost.

components.description: Every bound computed for this track, keyed by method name. The reported value is the maximum over the PROVABLE ones, since the maximum of valid bounds is valid.

conditional_components.description: Components recorded but NOT used to set `value`, because they are believed to bound the optimum without being proved to. `raw_best_known_conditional` is the motivating case: the per-family domination argument rests on the centreline-versus-arc costing convention being exact, which is not proved.

audit.description: Every input to the geometric floor, echoed so the value can be re-derived from this record alone -- no grid, no metadata, no code. validate.py re-derives it from metadata.json and fails on any mismatch.
